conversation_context.content: I'm instrumenting a Python agent by hand. How can I attach env='staging' to just one turn in its trace?

Call `set_attributes()` on that turn's `Turn` object, inside the `with weave.start_turn(...)` block. This stamps the attributes on that one span [S1].

```python
import weave

weave.init("[TEAM-NAME]/[PROJECT-NAME]")

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent"):
    with weave.start_turn(user_message="What is the weather in Tokyo?") as turn:
        turn.set_attributes({"env": "staging"})
```

This pattern follows the documentation's example, which sets `user_id`, `tenant`, and `env` on a turn [S1]. I haven't run it, because the offline sandbox has no Weave SDK.

Things to know:
- **Timing:** Set the attribute while the span is recording, which in Python means inside the `with` block. If you call `set_attributes()` before the span starts or after it ends, the call does nothing and logs a warning. It is silent only if OTel isn't installed or Weave is disabled [S2].
- **Scope:** `set_attributes()` tags only that span. The same method exists on the other span classes, for example `tool.set_attributes(...)` on a tool call [S1]. The docs also have a separate section on conversation-wide attributes. I didn't read it, so I can't describe how it works.
- **Key names:** Weave reserves the `weave.*` and `gen_ai.*` prefixes for special handling. For your own metadata, use custom keys. The docs give `user_id` and `tenant` as examples of keys stored as filterable custom attributes [S1]. `env` is a custom key of the same kind, but the docs don't name it specifically.
- **Batch logging:** If you log finished activity in one batch instead of live, the docs say to populate the span object's declared fields directly and pass the object to `log_turn` or `log_conversation` [S2]. I didn't read that page, so I can't give details.

Don't confuse this with `weave.attributes()`. That context manager is documented for functions traced with `@weave.op`. For agents instrumented with the Weave agent SDK, the docs point to attributes on agent spans (`Turn`, `LLM`, `Tool`, `SubAgent`) instead [S3].

# Set attributes and events on agent spans

> Attach custom attributes and record events on agent spans (Turn, LLM, Tool, and SubAgent) to filter and analyze agent activity in Weave.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/attributes-and-events).

When you instrument an agent with the Weave SDK, each span object (`Turn`, `LLM`, `Tool`, and `SubAgent`) exposes methods to attach custom metadata. Use these methods to stamp contextual information such as user IDs, tenants, experiment names, or environment labels onto agent spans, then filter and group agent activity by that metadata in the Weights & Biases UI.

This metadata comes in two forms:

* **Attributes**: Key-value properties of a span as a whole. Use `set_attributes()` (Python) or `setAttributes()` (TypeScript) to stamp attributes on a single span, or set conversation-wide attributes that apply to every span a conversation emits.
* **Events**: Point-in-time markers that occur during a span's lifetime, such as a permission prompt or a lifecycle transition. Use `add_event()` (Python) or `addEvent()` (TypeScript).

These methods mirror the [OpenTelemetry (OTel) span API](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-spans/): `set_attributes` mirrors OTel's `Span.set_attributes`, and `add_event` mirrors OTel's `Span.add_event`. The Weave SDK emits OTel spans and stores all attributes, so they remain queryable in Weave.

## When you can set attributes

Set attributes while the span is recording, that is, after the span starts and before it ends. In Python, this is inside the `with` block. In TypeScript, this is after `start*()` and before `end()`.

If you call `set_attributes()`, or its TypeScript equivalent on a span that hasn't started yet or has already ended, the call is a no-op and logs a warning that names the fix.

The call is silent (no warning) only when OTel isn't installed or Weave is disabled.

> [!TIP]
>
> To attach attributes when logging completed agent activity in a single batch rather than during live execution, populate the span object's declared fields directly and pass the object to `log_turn` or `log_conversation`. See [Log agent activity in batches](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents-batch.md).

# Define and log attributes

> Use attributes to add metadata to your traces and evaluations.

> [!NOTE]
>
> This page describes attributes for functions traced with the `@weave.op` decorator. If you instrument an agent with the Weave agent SDK, set attributes and events on agent spans (`Turn`, `LLM`, `Tool`, and `SubAgent`) instead. See [Set attributes and events on agent spans](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents-attributes.md).

Attributes in Weave let you attach custom metadata to your traces and evaluations. This metadata can include information like environment names, model versions, experiment IDs, user IDs, or other contextual information to help you organize, filter, and analyze your Weave data.

Attributes are especially helpful for grouping or filtering traces by:

* Deployments
* Tenants
* Experiments

Weave provides two ways to add attributes:

* **Per-call attributes**: Use the `weave.attributes()` context manager to add metadata to specific operations or code blocks.
* **Global attributes**: Use the `global_attributes` field to set attributes at initialization that apply to all traces and evaluations in your project.

You can view all attributes logged during traces and evaluations in the UI. You can then use them to filter and group data.

This guide is for Weave users who want to enrich their traces and evaluations with custom metadata. It covers how to attach attributes to individual calls, set project-wide defaults at initialization, combine the two approaches, and read the current attribute set during execution.

# Set attributes and events on agent spans

> Attach custom attributes and record events on agent spans (Turn, LLM, Tool, and SubAgent) to filter and analyze agent activity in Weave.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/attributes-and-events).

When you instrument an agent with the Weave SDK, each span object (`Turn`, `LLM`, `Tool`, and `SubAgent`) exposes methods to attach custom metadata. Use these methods to stamp contextual information such as user IDs, tenants, experiment names, or environment labels onto agent spans, then filter and group agent activity by that metadata in the Weights & Biases UI.

This metadata comes in two forms:

* **Attributes**: Key-value properties of a span as a whole. Use `set_attributes()` (Python) or `setAttributes()` (TypeScript) to stamp attributes on a single span, or set conversation-wide attributes that apply to every span a conversation emits.
* **Events**: Point-in-time markers that occur during a span's lifetime, such as a permission prompt or a lifecycle transition. Use `add_event()` (Python) or `addEvent()` (TypeScript).

These methods mirror the [OpenTelemetry (OTel) span API](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-spans/): `set_attributes` mirrors OTel's `Span.set_attributes`, and `add_event` mirrors OTel's `Span.add_event`. The Weave SDK emits OTel spans and stores all attributes, so they remain queryable in Weave.

## When you can set attributes

Set attributes while the span is recording, that is, after the span starts and before it ends. In Python, this is inside the `with` block. In TypeScript, this is after `start*()` and before `end()`.

If you call `set_attributes()`, or its TypeScript equivalent on a span that hasn't started yet or has already ended, the call is a no-op and logs a warning that names the fix.

The call is silent (no warning) only when OTel isn't installed or Weave is disabled.

> [!TIP]
>
> To attach attributes when logging completed agent activity in a single batch rather than during live execution, populate the span object's declared fields directly and pass the object to `log_turn` or `log_conversation`. See [Log agent activity in batches](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents-batch.md).

# Define and log attributes

> Use attributes to add metadata to your traces and evaluations.

> [!NOTE]
>
> This page describes attributes for functions traced with the `@weave.op` decorator. If you instrument an agent with the Weave agent SDK, set attributes and events on agent spans (`Turn`, `LLM`, `Tool`, and `SubAgent`) instead. See [Set attributes and events on agent spans](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents-attributes.md).

Attributes in Weave let you attach custom metadata to your traces and evaluations. This metadata can include information like environment names, model versions, experiment IDs, user IDs, or other contextual information to help you organize, filter, and analyze your Weave data.

Attributes are especially helpful for grouping or filtering traces by:

* Deployments
* Tenants
* Experiments

Weave provides two ways to add attributes:

* **Per-call attributes**: Use the `weave.attributes()` context manager to add metadata to specific operations or code blocks.
* **Global attributes**: Use the `global_attributes` field to set attributes at initialization that apply to all traces and evaluations in your project.

You can view all attributes logged during traces and evaluations in the UI. You can then use them to filter and group data.

This guide is for Weave users who want to enrich their traces and evaluations with custom metadata. It covers how to attach attributes to individual calls, set project-wide defaults at initialization, combine the two approaches, and read the current attribute set during execution.

# Set attributes and events on agent spans

> Attach custom attributes and record events on agent spans (Turn, LLM, Tool, and SubAgent) to filter and analyze agent activity in Weave.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/attributes-and-events).

When you instrument an agent with the Weave SDK, each span object (`Turn`, `LLM`, `Tool`, and `SubAgent`) exposes methods to attach custom metadata. Use these methods to stamp contextual information such as user IDs, tenants, experiment names, or environment labels onto agent spans, then filter and group agent activity by that metadata in the Weights & Biases UI.

This metadata comes in two forms:

* **Attributes**: Key-value properties of a span as a whole. Use `set_attributes()` (Python) or `setAttributes()` (TypeScript) to stamp attributes on a single span, or set conversation-wide attributes that apply to every span a conversation emits.
* **Events**: Point-in-time markers that occur during a span's lifetime, such as a permission prompt or a lifecycle transition. Use `add_event()` (Python) or `addEvent()` (TypeScript).

These methods mirror the [OpenTelemetry (OTel) span API](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-spans/): `set_attributes` mirrors OTel's `Span.set_attributes`, and `add_event` mirrors OTel's `Span.add_event`. The Weave SDK emits OTel spans and stores all attributes, so they remain queryable in Weave.

## When you can set attributes

Set attributes while the span is recording, that is, after the span starts and before it ends. In Python, this is inside the `with` block. In TypeScript, this is after `start*()` and before `end()`.

If you call `set_attributes()`, or its TypeScript equivalent on a span that hasn't started yet or has already ended, the call is a no-op and logs a warning that names the fix.

The call is silent (no warning) only when OTel isn't installed or Weave is disabled.

> [!TIP]
>
> To attach attributes when logging completed agent activity in a single batch rather than during live execution, populate the span object's declared fields directly and pass the object to `log_turn` or `log_conversation`. See [Log agent activity in batches](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents-batch.md).

# Define and log attributes

> Use attributes to add metadata to your traces and evaluations.

> [!NOTE]
>
> This page describes attributes for functions traced with the `@weave.op` decorator. If you instrument an agent with the Weave agent SDK, set attributes and events on agent spans (`Turn`, `LLM`, `Tool`, and `SubAgent`) instead. See [Set attributes and events on agent spans](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents-attributes.md).

Attributes in Weave let you attach custom metadata to your traces and evaluations. This metadata can include information like environment names, model versions, experiment IDs, user IDs, or other contextual information to help you organize, filter, and analyze your Weave data.

Attributes are especially helpful for grouping or filtering traces by:

* Deployments
* Tenants
* Experiments

Weave provides two ways to add attributes:

* **Per-call attributes**: Use the `weave.attributes()` context manager to add metadata to specific operations or code blocks.
* **Global attributes**: Use the `global_attributes` field to set attributes at initialization that apply to all traces and evaluations in your project.

You can view all attributes logged during traces and evaluations in the UI. You can then use them to filter and group data.

This guide is for Weave users who want to enrich their traces and evaluations with custom metadata. It covers how to attach attributes to individual calls, set project-wide defaults at initialization, combine the two approaches, and read the current attribute set during execution.

## When you can set attributes

Set attributes while the span is recording, that is, after the span starts and before it ends. In Python, this is inside the `with` block. In TypeScript, this is after `start*()` and before `end()`.

The call is silent (no warning) only when OTel isn't installed or Weave is disabled.

You can view all attributes logged during traces and evaluations in the UI. You can then use them to filter and group data.

This guide is for Weave users who want to enrich their traces and evaluations with custom metadata. It covers how to attach attributes to individual calls, set project-wide defaults at initialization, combine the two approaches, and read the current attribute set during execution.
